name: Gone but Not Forgotten: Dead Media and Lost Gadgets
description: Betamax tapes, floppy disks, MiniDiscs, teletext and typewriters: the formats and machines that ruled their day, then faded or gave way to digital successors.

checkpoints.name: Before the electronic age
checkpoints.note: The slide rule, signal towers, early photographs and one-penny stamps served well for a time. The typewriter, record cylinder and typesetting machine lasted for decades before better methods replaced them.

checkpoints.name: The first half of the century
checkpoints.note: Mechanical television with its spinning disc, Kodachrome colour film and Loran navigation belonged to a world that moved quickly and left some inventions behind.

checkpoints.name: Tapes and format wars
checkpoints.note: Eight-track tapes, Betamax, VHS and LaserDisc fought over the living room, teletext brought text to television, and in 1979 the cassette Walkman put music in a pocket. Format wars left winners, losers and drawers full of tapes.

checkpoints.name: The digital takeover
checkpoints.note: Minitel, MiniDisc, floppy disks, Zip drives, the Discman and GeoCities: all failed or gave way to digital successors, as phones and the internet absorbed what single machines once did.
